# Maintained dependency snapshots

The `native-clipboard-writer-v1` patch adds `ui.Content.WithClipboardWriter`, a per-content main-thread text-copy hook. Arion uses it for clipboard picker and text-selection copies so keyboard and system-menu selection copies carry the same internal marker as explicit copy buttons. It preserves selection, edit menus, and the default writer in other windows. Run `GOWORK=off CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./ui -run 'ContentClipboardWriter|TextSelection'` from `third_party/mygo`.

`mygo/` is the complete Go module snapshot of `github.com/egoist/mygo v0.4.6`, under its original MIT licence. `mygo-upstream-sha256.json` records every original module file's SHA-256 before patching. The desktop's `go.mod` replaces that dependency with this directory; the module cache is never modified. Package notices identify the local patch.

The `prerelease-channel-v1` patch adds `Updater.CheckWithOptions` and `UpdateCheckOptions.IncludePrereleases`. GitHub channel checks resolve published releases through the existing resolver, always exclude drafts and prereleases without a manifest for the running platform, and expose `ErrNoPublishedUpdates` separately from transport errors. The ordinary `Check` API retains its existing behavior. Signature validation and archive/delta formats are unchanged. `App.Version()` prefers the linked complete semantic version over macOS's numeric bundle version, while preserving explicit overrides.

The `url-channel-v1` patch extends `CheckWithOptions` to URL feeds (`updates.url`): the manifest request carries `channel=stable`, or `channel=beta` when prereleases are included, and a `404` from the channel server is `ErrNoPublishedUpdates`. The ordinary `Check` API still reports a `404` as a failure and sends no query. Arion's center serves these channels ([updates service](../services/updates/README.md)).

The `windows-update-rollback-v1` patch tracks newly added update entries alongside replaced entries. If a later replacement fails, rollback removes added files/directories as well as restoring the previous files, while retaining installer-owned entries absent from the update archive. Native Windows regressions hold a target file open through the replacement retry budget and verify the complete rollback, then replace a running PE executable and verify relaunch and old-file cleanup. The staged updater preserves that rollback contract in signed `Prepare` → `Apply` → `Acknowledge` regressions, including retained completion-receipt cleanup. The [alpha.16 release CI](https://github.com/AstraFoundry/Arion/actions/runs/40286770150) passes these regressions on `windows-2022`, including running-PE replacement, relaunch cleanup and locked-target rollback. Real antivirus interference and production-channel upgrade acceptance remain separate.

The `codesign-metadata-v1` patch removes `com.apple.FinderInfo` and `com.apple.ResourceFork` recursively before nested signing and again before the outer signature. Finder/file-provider metadata can appear on freshly copied Swift resource bundles. Cleanup uses the system `xattr`, preserves unrelated attributes, does not follow resource symlinks and fails explicitly on errors. Read-only generated resources are temporarily made owner-writable and their original modes are restored before signing, including on cleanup failure. Both development and production builds use this signing boundary. The patch also adds `mygo dev -out <directory>` (relative to the project or absolute, default `.mygo/dev`) so Arion can keep development bundles outside file-provider synchronization, which otherwise reattaches metadata after signing. Run `GOWORK=off CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./cmd/mygo -run 'TestSignNestedCode|TestNestedCodesignArgs|TestPackagingArgs|TestDevOutputDir|TestDevLaunch' -count=1` from `third_party/mygo` on macOS for the native regressions, including deliberate metadata contamination, read-only resources, strict signature verification and development output/lifecycle.

The `dev-build-only-v1` patch adds `mygo dev -build-only`, which compiles and signs the development bundle without launching it, running a dev server, or starting a watcher. Arion uses it on macOS and opens the resulting bundle through LaunchServices. Directly spawning the executable from a terminal or coding agent can attribute TCC requests to that parent instead of the app. `GOWORK=off CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./cmd/mygo -run 'TestDevBuildOnlyDoesNotLaunch|TestDevLaunch|TestDevOutputDir' -count=1` verifies the build artifact and absence of an app launch. Real permission attribution remains a native acceptance check.

The `windows-native-transparency-v1` patch routes transparent native windows through DirectComposition for both CPU frames and GPU swap chains. Creation fails explicitly when composition is unavailable, rather than displaying an opaque rectangle. It also preserves keyboard focus when a surface on a `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE` window accepts a pointer action. From `mygo`, run `MYGO_E2E=1 GOWORK=off CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./internal/windows -run TransparentSurface -count=1 -v` in an unlocked Windows desktop session. The regression samples actual desktop pixels, checks OS click-through hit testing, delivers owned native mouse messages without stealing focus, and verifies CPU composition-device recovery and GPU presentation. Physical mouse injection remains separate acceptance evidence.

The `staged-update-v1` patch adds `Update.Prepare(ctx, progress)` and `PreparedUpdate.Apply`, `Discard`, `Path`, `Version`, `Applied`, and `Acknowledge`. Preparation verifies the existing signed archive or delta and extracts beside the installation without replacing files. `Install` remains a compatibility composition of preparation and apply. `App.RelaunchWithResult` reports a vetoed quit so the application can retain its maintenance lease and retry safely; quit acceptance does not prove that the new process launched. Applications own consent, cancellation/generation and input/resource gates: apply is an uncancellable transaction and must run only inside the protected restart sequence. It replaces resources on disk, so continued resource loading by the old host is unsafe.

The bounded versioned staging record preserves target identity, manifest metadata, and tree digests. `Updater.RecoverPrepared(path)` checks this build's target and built-in key, verifies the retained signed artifact, reconstructs its expected tree, and compares the staged and installed trees before reuse. Application state must additionally bind the handle to its selected channel and version. Apply repeats these checks, obtains exclusive OS file-lock ownership and writes each rename's intent before moving files. A stable hidden ownership directory and its journal pointer remain beside the installation; kernel ownership releases on process exit while an interrupted journal still blocks replacement. A swap failure restores old entries and removes newly added entries; rollback failures retain the stage, backups and ownership journal and return `ErrUpdateRecoveryRequired` with the journal path. An interrupted transaction is refused for inspection rather than reused or deleted. This is failed-swap recovery, not a release health check or an unattended crash repair mechanism. Successful apply retains its completion receipt, signed source and old files until the application durably clears its saved handle and calls `Acknowledge`. `RecoverPrepared` also returns `Applied()==true` for a completed transaction only after verifying installed bytes against the signed artifact; deltas reconstruct their expected output from preserved old files. This closes the crash window between replacement and application-state persistence. On Windows, acknowledged backups held open by the old process retain their record and are cleaned on a later launch. The ownership subprocess regression checks automatic kernel unlock after termination and completed-receipt reconciliation on the current OS. Native Windows interruption/locked-file acceptance remains required.

Run `node scripts/check-updater.mjs --native` on a logged-in macOS desktop to build isolated ad-hoc-signed fixture bundles and exercise the actual native `App.Run` lifecycle: prepare leaves v1 resources intact, a second process recovers and applies the stage, `App.Relaunch` starts v2, reads v2 resources and reconciles the retained completion receipt before acknowledgement, and an invalid-signature fixture remains at v1. It only replaces temporary fixture bundles. The test does not establish production signing/notarization, Windows acceptance, or Arion's input/worker coordination.

Run `make updater-check` or `pnpm updater:check` for upstream updater/signature/install tests plus GitHub/URL channel and staged preparation, tampering, cancellation, ownership, rollback and recovery regressions. Native application tests cover preference persistence, stale-check invalidation and the independent settings switch. When upgrading MyGo, compare the recorded original bytes, rebase the patch and run these gates before replacing the snapshot.


The `native-notifications-v1` patch separates notification authorization query/request from submission, forwards bounded body/custom action identifiers, and removes stable IDs across process lifetimes. macOS requests silent alert authorization explicitly, registers native action categories, attaches its delegate during launch and invalidates asynchronous submissions on removal. Windows replaces tray balloons with OS WinRT toast, a stable AUMID/derived COM activator, a bounded singleton activation relay and per-user NSIS shortcut/COM install/uninstall registration. `windows.notifications` opts packaging into the installer entry point; Arion enables it. No Windows App SDK runtime or other runtime dependency is added. Applications still own fixed action routing, localized copy and stale channel/version policy.

Run `pnpm notifications:check` for the complete wire-format suite, public API/permission/action/installer regressions and Windows amd64/arm64 cross-builds. Windows-only COM factory/queue and actual shortcut-property tests are in `internal/windows/notify_test.go`; execute them on Windows with `GOWORK=off CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./internal/windows -run Notification -count=1` from the snapshot. `node scripts/check-notifications.mjs --native` builds an isolated sender and runs its real packaged query/cleanup lifecycle; `--interactive` requires actual native warm/cold action interaction. It never modifies Arion's production sender or private notification databases.

Local macOS arm64 probe observations establish unknown authorization without a prompt, refusal of an unauthorized `Show` without a prompt, the owned sender's native authorization prompt and allowed result, current enabled settings and accepted submissions, followed by an owned clear request and observed process exit. A local permission-settings screenshot and JSONL events are retained under ignored `.workspace/e2e/notifications/current/`. Actual banner visibility and warm/cold action callbacks did not complete through the available Notification Center UI surface and remain unverified. Windows registration, sender identity, COM activation, upgrade/uninstall and native callback tests have only cross-build evidence here; they require real Windows execution. Do not treat submission or cross-compilation as those acceptance results.

The `screen-anchored-flyout-v1` patch adds `FlyoutOptions.ScreenAnchor` for an independent native panel anchored in screen DIPs. It reuses the existing flyout lifecycle, keyboard focus and monitor placement without activating the application on macOS. Windows converts the selected monitor's DIPs to physical pixels; X11 places the independent utility window and Wayland retains compositor control. Parent/tray flyouts keep their existing behavior. Run `GOWORK=off CGO_ENABLED=0 go test . ./internal/platform -run 'Flyout|WorkArea|Display' -count=1` from `mygo`; Arion's `TestClipboardInForeignFullscreenSpace` covers the production macOS fullscreen behavior.
